scope: Make GitHub native issue dependencies the sole authority for blocked-by relationships. Add an exact `BLOCKED` option to the project Disposition field and derive that transient value from whether any native dependency has not reached AITM Status `Done`; clear Disposition when all dependencies are Done while retaining the relationships as provenance. Preserve the existing blocker gates on every forward transition from Ready for Planning through Review and make `pull-next` dependency-aware. Make `aitm block` an idempotent set union and `aitm unblock --by` an idempotent set subtraction, with an explicit remove-all form. Reconcile eagerly on block/unblock and AITM Done, and lazily on bind, `pull-next`, and guarded transitions. Provide a dry-run/apply migration for strict legacy markers on open issues, then retire legacy marker, `Blocked By` field, and `BLOCKED` label writes and provisioning. Do not add a webhook, background daemon, commit hook, destructive project-field deletion, or automatic migration of ambiguous label-only state.
acs: The canonical Disposition definition contains exact option `BLOCKED`, and installation/repair adds it without changing existing option identities or values.

Native GitHub `blockedBy` and `blocking` relationships are the sole runtime dependency authority; blocker body markers, the `Blocked By` project field, and the `BLOCKED` label are no longer written or provisioned.
`aitm block [A] --by B,C` performs an idempotent set union, preserves unrelated dependencies, rejects invalid/self dependencies, and reconciles A's Disposition from the verified native set.

`aitm unblock [A] --by B` performs an idempotent set subtraction, preserves unrelated dependencies, supports explicit remove-all when `--by` is omitted, and reconciles Disposition from the remaining native set.

A dependent issue has Disposition `BLOCKED` when any native dependency is not AITM Done and an empty Disposition when all dependencies are Done or none exist; unreadable dependency state fails closed and terminal Disposition values are never overwritten or cleared.
Native dependencies gate every existing forward exit from Ready for Planning through Review, and `pull-next` does not select a child with any unfinished or unreadable dependency.

An AITM Done transition eagerly reconciles issues named by the completed issue's native `blocking` relationships without removing satisfied relationships; bind, block/unblock, `pull-next`, and guarded transitions lazily repair stale Disposition values.

`aitm migrate-dependencies --dry-run|--apply` converts verified strict legacy markers on open issues, is interruption-safe and idempotent, leaves closed history untouched, and reports ambiguous label-only state without mutating it.
Documentation and tests describe native dependency authority, set semantics, feature-branch Done satisfaction, projection clearing, failure recovery, and the no-webhook operational boundary.
